text:
aj: FYI seeing a new regression in streamed responses after yesterday's kernel-orchestrator change. Short chatty replies spike latency and occasionally time out when KV cache is cold. Repro: burst of small streaming requests -> some late flushes ~200-400ms beyond SLO. :eyes:
kevin: can you paste the exact config you ran? and a quick profile?
maria: linking perf-bot output, looks like batch formation + partial-decode preemption is stalling some streams. perf-bot: https://internal.perf/graphs/stream-surges/3009876543 :point_up:
aj: config snippet (sanitized):
```
serve.runtime.batch.min_batch_wait_ms=6
serve.runtime.batch.max_batch_tokens=2048
serve.runtime.stream.flush_cadence_ms=20
serve.runtime.stream.partial_decode_preempt=true
serve.runtime.batch.token_budget_target=0.75
```
aj: observed behaviour: small requests pile up, kernel-selection picks large-kernel path for a couple, then partial-decode preempt tries to slice but flush cadence interacts with the coalesce window so some streams miss the early-send event. Also KV cache warms but those requests were assigned after warmup and then starved by greedy batch builders.
sophie: do we have traces showing which code path delayed the flush? kernel handoff vs batcher timer?
maria: trace shows delay at "batch_coalesce.go:142" waiting for token budget decision. The preempt handshake sometimes yields to a long-running decode on same GPU. Flamegraph (perf-bot): top functions are batch_coalesce, kernel_select, partial_decode_scheduler.
kevin: my hunch: token_budget_target too aggressive for mixed small-chat workload. With target 0.75 the batcher waits for more tokens before flush if any request is large-ish. For streams we should bias toward earlier flush or prioritize stream-first admission.
nate: we could try: (1) separate stream admission queue with lower min_batch_wait_ms, (2) reduce token_budget_target for stream-eligible batches, or (3) preempt long non-stream decodes to free the kernel for stream partial-decodes.
aj: propose quick experiment A/B: variant A = stream_queue=true + stream_min_batch_wait_ms=2, token_budget_target_stream=0.5. variant B = keep config but enable preemptive-kernel-yield for stream partial decodes. Measure p50/p95/p99 latency for streamed responses and token cost delta.
maria: add metrics: stream_early_send_rate, stream_late_flush_rate, kv_miss_pct, kernel_preempt_yields. perf-bot will collect flamegraphs per canary.
kevin: small note: need to handle KV cache warmup bias. If stream requests land on GPUs with cold KV, preempting helps but we also need to avoid ping-pong of warm kernels. Maybe add sticky affinity for stream replays for N seconds.
sophie: +1 on sticky affinity. Also suggest increasing stream.flush_cadence_ms to 30ms temporarily to reduce churn if partial decodes trigger many small kernels. But that may increase latency for truly tiny responses.
aj: tradeoffs noted. For low-p95 we need earlier sends, for p99 we want preemption. We'll run both experiments 1 hour each on canary pool.
maria: I'm pushing a perf job now. perf-bot: start job job_id=sr-3009876543-exp, will run 1h canary across 10% capacity and produce perf logs.
perf-bot: job sr-3009876543-exp started. collecting metrics: stream_early_send_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, token_cost_per_1000. linking dashboard: https://internal.perf/dash/sr-3009876543-exp
kevin: I'll sketch change for preemptive-kernel-yield. simple flag: serve.runtime.stream.preemptive_kernel_yield=true, threshold_ms=80 (if decode running > threshold yield to partial-decode).
nate: I'll own canary rollout. scheduling canary window at 11:30 PDT. Adding rollout note to eng-runtime on-call.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled by nate at 2026-03-18T11:30:00-07:00. Targets: canary-pool-1 (10%). Auto-rollback on stream_late_flush_rate increase > 10% or p99 latency increase > 15%.\sophie: quick reminder: add a guard to avoid preempt thrashing: cooldown per GPU 500ms.
aj: good call. I'll add cooldown and sticky affinity. After perf run we'll reconvene. Thanks all :thumbsup:
maria: initial perf snapshot (10m): p50=12ms, p95=48ms, p99=180ms, stream_late_flush_rate=6%, kv_miss_pct=22%. Baseline before change p99 was ~120ms. so regression visible.
kevin: ok that's actionable. If A/B shows preempt reduces p99 without cost explosion in token usage, we ship. If token cost up >20% revert.
ate: logging follow-up: adding debug counter for "preempt_yield_count" and "sticky_affinity_hits".
aj: assigned owners: kev -> preempt code, nate -> rollout, maria -> perf collection, sophie -> monitoring alert thresholds. Meeting in #eng-runtime in 45m for results.
deploy-bot: Canary completed: no rollbacks triggered. Waiting for perf-bot final report.
perf-bot: sr-3009876543-exp results: A (stream_queue + token_budget_stream=0.5): p99=95ms (-47%), token_cost +12%. B (preemptive_kernel_yield): p99=88ms (-51%), token_cost +18%. stream_late_flush_rate dropped to 1.8% (A) and 1.2% (B).
aj: B looks promising but cost delta close to threshold. propose rollout with cost cap flag and autoscale token_budget_target when sustained cost>15%.\eof
